newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos to leave hospital Sunday, told to slow down.
newsitem.headline: Ramos to leave hospital Sunday, told to slow down.

text.p: Philippine president Fidel Ramos will leave hospital on Sunday after resting for a full day and taking medication for a throat infection, but his doctor said on Saturday he needs to take it easy.
"He's okay now. He's going home tomorrow," Raul Fores, medical director of the Makati Medical Centre, told reporters.
Fores denied reports in some local newspapers saying Ramos had suffered a mild stroke.
"You don't send him home in three days. No, no," Fores said, commenting on the reports. "That's definite."
He said he had advised Ramos to meet some reporters to dispel the speculation. On Friday, Fores said Ramos was "suffering from nothing more serious than a flu".

Ramos, a 68-year-old workaholic who also jogs and plays golf regularly, was admitted to the hospital on Thursday night complaining of pains in his joints. He checked himself out on Friday to attend two functions, including a state dinner for Luxembourg's Prince Henri, but returned to the hospital later for further checks.
Fores said Ramos, who had a series of tests on his heart and prostate, was already feeling better..
"So far, all these checks are... okay," Fores said. "He's got to slow down. He's not resting enough... He is not young any more."
Ramos cancelled all his weekend plans, including a trip to southern Philippines, but was invited by doctors to join their Christmas party in the hospital later on Saturday.
Also in the hospital, on the same floor as Ramos, was former first lady Imelda Marcos, being treated for an eye ailment.
A Marcos aide said the widow of the late president Ferdinand Marcos sent Ramos a bouquet of roses with a card, reading: "I pray that the Lord gives you a clean bill of health."
Ramos was national police chief under Marcos until he helped lead a popular revolt in 1986 to end the former president's 20-year rule.
